# Template migrations

One entry per template version, newest first. An entry lists what a project must do to move from the previous version;
"nothing" is a valid entry. An entry is written so that it can be used as the brief of a run.

The `## Unreleased` entry comes first. A commit that changes a template-owned path adds its line there in the same
commit: the date, the path (or its folder, ending in `/`) and the step a project takes; the release moves the entry
under its version number. `ops/tests/test_migrations_entry.py` (run by `uv run pytest -q`) fails when a path changed
since the last release is not named in the entry, and when a commit made since then changes a template-owned path and
adds no line to the entry (one made before its line existed is named in the entry by its short sha, as the back-fill
lines do; uncommitted changes count as the commit in the making). Exempt: this file, `CHANGELOG.md`,
`docs/template/VERSION`, the `omit:` prefixes of `docs/template/variables.yaml` and the template's generated records
(`.raw/`, `wiki/meta/`, `wiki/index.md`, `wiki/log.md`, `wiki/hot.md`). In a project's checkout (it keeps
`docs/template/README.md`) the test skips.

  there and move the old `<repo_name>-runs/` content into its `runs/`; `git worktree repair`; remove the moved `.venv`
  (it keeps the old paths) and run `python3 ops/bootstrap.py --wait`; accept Claude Code's trust dialog in the new
  folder.

- Changed template-owned paths: {list}
